And there reigned in Egypt that fourth king of the Shepherds:
Apophis,
for fourteen years.
This is he who dreamed the dreams and gave Joseph authority,

And it is likely

After Levi, Kohath his son.
At the age of sixty years he begat Amram.

After Kohath, Amram his son.
At the age of seventy-five (or seventy-seven) years he begat Moses, in the year three hundred and fifty of the Promise.
All his life was one hundred and thirty-seven years.
And in his days there reigned in Egypt Maphres for twelve years,
and then Thomothes for eighteen years,
and then Amenophis for forty-three years.
This one began drowning the male children of the Hebrews in the Nile.
After Amram, Moses his son.
He was appointed over the children of Israel at eighty years of age,
and led the people in the wilderness for forty years.
When he was born,
he was cast into the river.
And the daughter of Pharaoh Amenophis,
whose name was Tremothisa,
who is Reosa (Ra'mosa?),
whom the Hebrews call Damaris,
the wife of Chenephres king of Memphis,
found him and drew him out of the water,
and reared him for herself as a son.
And when he was ten years old, Jannes and Jambres taught him wisdom,
as Artapanus showed in a letter.
In the Law, however, this is not written,
but Paul the Apostle mentions it.
And in the twenty-second year of Pharaoh Amenophis himself, he began to oppress {OCR?} the Hebrews to make bricks and to build the city of Hermopolis.
And he also conquered the Ethiopians,
and took Reosa, the daughter of Sorus (Zorus) their king, as a wife.
Some, however, attribute this victory to Moses,
and say that he married this Reosa,
